items.q: Which of these is NOT synthesisable into hardware?
options: #10 a = b; inside an always block
items.explain: Delay controls like #10 are only for simulation; synthesis tools ignore or reject them because real delay comes from the gates, not the code.

items.q: A synchronous FIFO has 16 entries but its read and write pointers are 5 bits wide instead of 4. Why the extra bit?
options: To count how many reads have happened
To tell full from empty when the lower 4 bits are equal
items.explain: Both full and empty have equal lower pointer bits; the extra MSB differs when the write pointer has wrapped once more than the read pointer, which means full.

items.q: A UART transmitter runs from a 50 MHz clock and must send at 115200 baud. What value should the baud-tick counter divide by?
items.explain: 50,000,000 / 115,200 = 434.03, so one bit lasts 434 clock cycles.

items.q: In SystemVerilog, which always block tells the tool you intend a flip-flop and warns if the code cannot be one?
items.explain: always_ff declares sequential intent, so the tool checks for a clock edge and flags accidental combinational or latch behaviour.
